title: Lunar Drift (Vibe coded Battlezone 1998)
author: ChampionshipComplex
selftext:
Three evenings of Codex, starting without even a compiler or unity + AI managed to help me create a fairly good rendition of a 1990s Game I loved called Battlezone.

Worked on the terrain first, and vehicle physics + Only got good once I stopped AI from trying to simulate a hovering motion and instead made it focus on actually putting thrusters on the vehicle in 5 directions and then working out the game mechanics. 

The terrain map is 256km square , which I created with AI joining up terrain maps of Idaho and Wales in the UK. 

Its strange how the things that I thought would be hard, like vehicle paths, or getting ships to shoot at each other - just seemed to happen with barely any input from me.

The hardest thing in all 3 evenings of doing this, was and still is, trying to make the font look readable on a cockpit control panel which is at an angle from your viewpoint.

comments.author: TheFlyingSheeps
comments.body: How did you make the cockpit and control panel?

replies.author: ChampionshipComplex
replies.body:
The below was pretty much the cockpit that Codex created straight out of the gate - 

https://i.redd.it/io8916k4ee3i1.png

Literally to get to the above level of game in this screenshot took just ten prompts. 

I had to get it to make the cockpit move as a 3D object to give you the sense of acceleration  - but that's basically what I said to it. The mesh on the left I had to tune a little but the hardest bit was getting it to put the compass headings on it. 

While the newer cockpit has less going on, I spent some time trying to get it to add more textures, and a feeling of physical space. I shared with Codex pictures of actual cockpits - Im still not happy with it, but at least I have 9 fixed display areas to at least have future readouts go to the correct screen.
